svg.title: Temporary Shields vs Permanent Patching: Kernel BPF, Java Startup Agents, and PHP Containment
svg.desc: Comparison diagram in two parts. Top row shows Shirudo's five-step temporary mitigation lifecycle: vulnerability disclosure while permanent patch is tested, operator signing an ML-DSA-87 upatch, target loading and measuring the shield in the vTPM register (delivered via workstation SSH relay or Azure VM Run Command), rolling out the real upstream patch, and removing the temporary shield with a signed payload-matched unload directive. Bottom row compares three shipped shield mechanisms by verification path, activation timing, and security boundary: Kernel BPF upatches (kernel keyring check, live BPF attach without kernel reboot while task-labeled sandboxes enter on next exec, pinned lsm/bpf denying unsigned BPF loads, map edits, and link detaches during this boot, not a boot or Azure-admin boundary), Java agent upatches (userspace signature check, Premain-Class JAR wired via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS at JVM startup, inside-JVM mitigation), and PHP app-sandbox containment (kernel BPF LSM restricts child execve, network egress, and .php file writes after compromise without fixing the underlying PHP bug).
